key_insight: An adaptive, moving phase-field solver uses gradient smoothing on a layered structured mesh to concentrate resolution only near evolving interfaces while keeping bulk regions coarse.
engineering_relevance: This makes large-scale interface simulations in solid mechanics and materials modeling much cheaper without sacrificing second-order accuracy where the interface matters most.
method: Couples the Gradient Smoothing Method (GSM) with hierarchical adaptive/moving structured meshes.
Uses layered refinement to keep the interfacial region locally uniform and accurately resolved.
Retains coarse discretization in bulk domains to reduce total degrees of freedom and improve scaling.
evidence_signal: Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard tests show the adaptive GSM solver achieves the desired interface accuracy with near-linear O(N) computational complexity versus the quadratic scaling of uniform-grid approaches.
watch_item: GSM has a higher cost per degree of freedom than standard finite differences, so performance depends on achieving enough adaptive reduction in mesh size.
paper_title: An adaptive phase field framework for large-scale interface evolution problems using a strong-form gradient smoothing approach
